# Local‑Pricing & Business‑Model Playbook **For:** Global Streaming Service – “the Company” **Date:** 23 August 2026 --- ## 1. Executive Overview | What investors care about | What the market demands | How we reconcile the two | |---------------------------|------------------------|--------------------------| | **Defensible consolidated unit economics** (CAC, LTV, contribution margin, EBITDA) | **Highly diverse income levels, payment habits and family‑sharing norms** in Africa, South‑Asia and Latin‑America | Build a **single‑price‑reference model** in USD, then *local‑price‑adjust* each market with transparent, data‑driven multipliers (PPP, elasticity, tax & FX). Convert back to USD at a **standardised “pricing‑exchange rate”** for reporting; keep the **margin envelope** identical to the USD‑reference (minus measured local cost differentials). | | **Predictable cash‑flow & low FX volatility** | **Mobile‑money, QR, instalments, prepaid “micro‑subs”** dominate | Offer **localized payment rails** that settle in local currency, but **auto‑convert** to USD at the day‑of‑settlement spot rate and hedge the net exposure (10‑day forwards, NDFs). | | **Scalable growth narrative** | **Family‑sharing & “group‑plans”** are cultural expectations; many households want a single subscription for 4‑6 users | Design a **modular family‑plan architecture** that can be priced as a multiple of the base tier (e.g., 1.75× for 4‑6 users) and treated as a **single contract** for CAC/LTV calculations. | | **Clear, comparable KPIs** | **Different plan cadences (weekly, monthly, quarterly, “pay‑as‑you‑go”)** | Standardise **effective monthly price** (EMP) for every transaction; all downstream financial models (ARPU, churn, LTV) work on EMP, not on the raw contract length. | The result is a **local‑first subscription experience** that still speaks the same “financial language” to the board and the investors. --- ## 2. Market Segmentation & Core Variables | Region | Typical Income (PPP‑adjusted) | Dominant Payment Rail | Household‑Sharing Norm | Attitude to Recurring Billing | |--------|------------------------------|-----------------------|------------------------|-------------------------------| | **Sub‑Saharan Africa (SSA)** | $2 k–$7 k PPP / yr | Mobile‑money (M‑Pay), USSD, QR, carrier‑billing | Large extended families; 4‑7 members per dwelling | Skeptical of automatic debit; prefer **pre‑paid / “pay‑as‑you‑go”** (weekly or 10‑day top‑ups). | | **East & South‑Asia** (e.g., India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka) | $3 k–$10 k PPP / yr | Mobile wallets (PayTM, Google Pay), QR, UPI, credit‑card “installments” | 3‑5 members, strong “family‑plan” culture (shared devices). | Comfortable with **auto‑renewal** if tied to mobile‑wallet/upi with OTP; but demand **grace‑period** for payment failures. | | **Latin America (LAT‑AM)** (Mexico, Colombia, Brazil, Peru, Chile) | $8 k–$18 k PPP / yr | Debit‑card, credit‑card, “cuotas” (installments), carrier‑billing (e.g., Vivo, Claro) | 2‑4 members, increasing “family‑bundle” demand. | Positive to **monthly recurring**, but expect **price‑freeze** and **transparent early‑cancellation**. | > **Key Insight:** The **price elasticity** in each region is driven more by **payment friction** than by raw price level. Removing friction (mobile‑money integration, prepaid buckets) yields a 20‑30 % lift in conversion for the same USD price. --- ## 3. Pricing Architecture – “USD‑Reference + Local Multiplier” ### 3.1. Core USD‑Reference Tier (Global) | Tier (USD) | Feature Set (global) | Target Global Gross Margin | |------------|----------------------|----------------------------| | **Basic** | SD‑only, 1 device, ads‑supported | 65 % | | **Standard** | HD, 2 devices, no ads | 68 % | | **Premium** | 4K, 4 devices, offline download | 70 % | These **reference prices** stay on the corporate balance sheet, *unchanged* across markets. ### 3.2. Local Multiplier Formula ``` Local Price (LC) = USD‑Reference × PPP‑Factor × Elasticity‑Factor × Tax‑Factor × FX‑Buffer ``` | Variable | Definition | Source | Typical Range | |----------|------------|--------|----------------| | **PPP‑Factor** | Ratio of local PPP (GDP per capita) to US PPP | World Bank, IMF | 0.12 – 0.55 | | **Elasticity‑Factor** | Adjusts for observed price‑elasticity (derived from A/B testing) | Internal pricing experiments | 0.8 – 1.3 | | **Tax‑Factor** | (1 + local VAT / digital‑services tax) | Local tax authority | 1.00 – 1.22 | | **FX‑Buffer** | Small cushion (1‑2 %) to absorb settlement‑day FX swing | Treasury | 1.00 – 1.02 | *All multipliers are **capped** so that the resulting **effective monthly price (EMP)** never falls below the **company‑wide floor** (c. $2.00 USD for Basic, $5 for Standard, $8 for Premium).* ### 3.3. Example – Kenya (SSA) | Input | Value | |------|-------| | USD‑Reference (Standard) | $5.00 | | PPP‑Factor (Kenya) | 0.18 | | Elasticity‑Factor (high mobile‑money friction) | 1.20 | | Tax‑Factor (VAT = 16 %) | 1.16 | | FX‑Buffer | 1.01 | | **Local Price (KES)** | **$5 × 0.18 × 1.20 × 1.16 × 1.01 ≈ $1.27 USD** → **KES ≈ 150** | Result: **150 KES / month** (≈ $1.27) – well above the $2 USD floor but affordable relative to PPP and reflects the added friction cost. --- ## 4. Payment‑Rail Integration & Cash‑Flow Design | Market | Preferred Rail | Settlement Path | FX Management | Revenue Recognition | |--------|----------------|----------------|--------------|---------------------| | **SSA** | Mobile‑money (M‑Pay, Airtel Money, M‑Pesa) | Direct settlement to local bank → auto‑convert via Treasury partner (e.g., Western Union Business Solutions) | 3‑day forward contracts locked at day‑of‑settlement spot | Recognise **monthly revenue** when service days are consumed (prorated for prepaid buckets). | | **South‑Asia** | UPI / QR wallets (PayTM, PhonePe), instalments (5‑month “cuotas”) | Aggregator settles in INR → Treasury converts to USD via NDFs (10‑day horizon) | Hedge 80 % of forecasted INR flow; leave 20 % un‑hedged for upside | Recognise revenue **ratably** across the contractual period (even for instalments). | | **LAT‑AM** | Debit/credit cards, carrier‑billing, “pay‑later” (Mercado Pago) | Card acquirer settles in local currency → Treasury FX forward | Use monthly rolling forwards; embed a **FX‑adjustment reserve** in the Income Statement (treated as other income/expense) | Same ratable treatment; carrier‑billing flagged as **deferred revenue** until period‑end. | **Why it works:** * The **company records all subscription revenue in USD** (the reporting currency) at the **spot rate of the day the payment is received**. * The **FX‑buffer** in the multiplier already covers the expected translation loss/gain, so the **gross margin** stays within the target band. * **Hedging** cushions the residual volatility; any residual translation gain/loss flows through a **FX‑adjustment line** that is *excluded* from EBITDA (EBITDA‑ex‑FX is the investor‑facing metric). --- ## 5. Family‑Sharing & Group‑Plan Mechanics | Plan Type | Base Tier | Max Users | Pricing Logic | Impact on Unit‑Economics | |-----------|-----------|-----------|----------------|--------------------------| | **Solo** | Any tier | 1 | USD‑Reference × Local Multiplier | Baseline CAC‑to‑LTV. | | **Family‑Plan (4‑6 users)** | Standard or Premium | 4‑6 | **1.75 ×** the solo EMP (rounded to nearest local‑currency increment) | CAC amortised over ~5 users → **LTV ↑ ≈ 2.5×**; marginal cost per extra user ≈ $0.30 USD (stream‑delivery bandwidth). | | **Mini‑Group (2‑3 users)** | Standard | 2‑3 | **1.3 ×** solo EMP | Useful in markets where 4‑user sharing is illegal (e.g., certain LAT‑AM consumer‑protection rules). | | **Pay‑As‑You‑Go / “Week‑Pass”** | Basic | 1 | Fixed **weekly price** = 0.25 × monthly EMP, prepaid and auto‑renewable via mobile cash‑out | Low CAC (no trial‑period churn), but higher churn; treat as **high‑frequency, low‑margin** cohort. | **Implementation notes** * **Account‑Linking:** Family plans are a **single legal contract** with a “primary payer” (usually the head of household). This keeps CAC accounting simple – the acquisition cost of the primary payer covers the whole group. * **Device Limits:** Enforce via device‑ID registration; extra devices beyond the limit can be added for a **$0.99 USD** per‑device surcharge (converted locally). * **Grace‑Period:** 5‑day grace for any payment failure before suspension; automatic downgrade to “Basic‑Free” (ad‑supported) after 14 days. --- ## 6. Consolidated Unit‑Economics Framework ### 6.1. Key Metric Definitions (All reported in **USD**) | Metric | Formula (per subscriber) | How it stays comparable | |--------|--------------------------|--------------------------| | **Effective Monthly Price (EMP)** | Σ (local‑price × conversion‑rate) ÷ months in contract | Normalises weekly, quarterly, prepaid plans. | | **Gross Margin %** | (EMP − Content‑Cost − CDN‑Cost − Payment‑Processing‑Fee) ÷ EMP | Payment‑processing fee is measured **in local currency**, then converted at settlement rate. | | **CAC (USD)** | Marketing spend ÷ **new paying** subscribers (incl. family‑plan primary) | Marketing spend is booked in USD; subscriber count is **post‑conversion** (each family plan counts as 1). | | **LTV (USD)** | Σ (EMP × Retention‑Rateⁿ) – Σ (CAC) | Retention rates are derived from **cohort analysis** on a **monthly‑effective** basis. | | **Contribution Margin** | LTV − CAC | Used for “Unit‑Economics KPI” presented to the board. | | **FX‑Adjustment (USD)** | (Spot‑Rate – Forward‑Rate) × Net‑Local‑Currency‑Revenue | Displayed separately; **EBITDA‑ex‑FX** = EBITDA + FX‑Adjustment. | ### 6.2. Margin Preservation Logic 1. **Target Gross Margin** = 66 % (global baseline). 2. **Local Cost Add‑Ons** (e.g., higher payment‑gateway fees in LAT‑AM, extra localisation licences) are **explicit line items** in the margin model. 3. The **PPP‑factor** and **Elasticity‑Factor** are calibrated **until** the EMP yields the target margin *after* those add‑ons. 4. **If a market’s true cost structure pushes margin below 60 %**, the pricing matrix automatically **raises the multiplier** (within the floor‑cap) to restore margin – the price increase is justified to investors as “cost‑driven localisation”. --- ## 7. Investor‑Ready Financial Model – “What‑If” Scenarios | Scenario | Change | Impact on Consolidated USD‑Revenue (12 m) | Impact on EBITDA‑ex‑FX | |----------|--------|--------------------------------------------|--------------------------| | **Base case** (current multipliers) | – | $1.20 B | $320 M | | **+10 % payment‑gateway fees in LAT‑AM** | Tax‑Factor ↑ 0.10 | +$12 M revenue (higher EMP) | EBITDA unchanged (margin preserved). | | **Currency devaluation – MXN 15 % vs USD** | FX‑Buffer 1.02 → 1.04 | $2 M translation loss, hedged 80 % → $1.6 M loss in FX‑Adjustment line (non‑EBITDA) | EBITDA‑ex‑FX +$1.6 M (still positive). | | **Introducing “Weekly Pass” in Kenya (15 % of users)** | New low‑price cohort (EMP ≈ $1.10) | +$8 M revenue (higher volume) | Gross margin drops 2 pp for that cohort → EBITDA‑ex‑FX -$4 M (acceptable if churn ≤ 8 %). | | **Family‑Plan uptake +20 pp in Brazil** | 1.75× price for 4‑6 users | +$30 M revenue (same CAC) | EBITDA‑ex‑FX +$18 M (margin improves). | **Bottom‑line:** The model shows **no scenario where localized pricing erodes the consolidated margin envelope**; any extra cost or FX movement is either *captured in the multiplier* or *isolated in the FX‑Adjustment line*. --- ## 8. Implementation Roadmap (18 months) | Phase | Timeline | Activities | Owner | |------|----------|------------|-------| | **1️⃣ Discovery & Data‑Science** | M0‑M3 | • Run price‑sensitivity tests (A/B) in 5 pilot cities (Nairobi, Mumbai, São Paulo).
• Build PPP‑elasticity regression model.
• Map payment‑rail partners & settlement processes. | Pricing & Analytics | | **2️⃣ Multiplier Engine Build** | M4‑M6 | • Deploy a **Pricing‑Multiplier Service** (micro‑service) that pulls live PPP, tax, and FX data via APIs.
• Integrate with subscription‑billing platform (Stripe, Adyen, local aggregators). | Engineering | | **3️⃣ Payment‑Rail Integration** | M5‑M9 | • Sign contracts with Mobile‑Money aggregators (M‑Pesa, Paytm, Mercado Pago).
• Implement **token‑ised** payment flow, auto‑conversion, and FX‑forward trigger. | Treasury + Ops | | **4️⃣ Product‑Launch – Tiered Plans** | M8‑M12 | • Publish **Local Pricing Catalog** in app/store (prices shown in local currency).
• Enable **Family‑Plan UI** (primary‑payer invite flow).
• Deploy weekly‑pass option in SSA pilots. | Product & Marketing | | **5️⃣ Monitoring & Hedge Execution** | M10‑M15 | • Launch **Consolidated Pricing Dashboard** (real‑time EMP, margin, FX exposure).
• Treasury begins systematic **10‑day forward hedging** for each currency bucket. | Finance | | **6️⃣ Full‑Scale Roll‑out** | M13‑M18 | • Expand to all target markets (total ~30 countries).
• Conduct “Price‑Lock” communications (e.g., “Your price stays the same for 12 months”).
• Quarterly Investor Briefings on **Localized‑Pricing KPI Pack**. | Global Ops | *Milestones include a **Go‑Live checklist** for each market (legal sign‑off, tax registration, payment‑gateway certification).* --- ## 9. Governance & Risk Management | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | |------|------------|--------|------------| | **FX volatility > 5 %** | Medium | Erosion of EBITDA‑ex‑FX | Hedge 80 % of net‑local‑currency revenue; maintain **FX‑adjustment reserve** (≤ 2 % of revenue). | | **Regulatory push‑back on family‑sharing (anti‑bundling rules)** | Low‑Medium (e.g., EU‑type “consumer‑choice” laws) | Potential re‑classification of plan as “multiple contracts” | Design family‑plan as **single legal contract** with internal “sub‑accounts”; ready legal fallback. | | **Payment‑gateway fraud spikes** | Medium (mobile‑money) | Revenue loss, brand damage | Deploy **real‑time risk scoring**, limit first‑time top‑ups, escrow‑hold 24 h for high‑risk cards. | | **Price‑parity complaints in high‑income markets** | Low | Reputation risk | Maintain **Uniform‑USD‑Reference** visible in “Pricing FAQ”; clearly state “local‑currency pricing reflects cost & income differences”. | | **Under‑pricing in ultra‑low‑income markets** (e.g., war‑torn regions) | Low | Loss of revenue per subscriber | Apply **minimum‑price floor** (USD $2) and/or **ad‑supported free tier** to keep brand presence. | **Governance board** – “Global Pricing & Localization Committee” (GPLC) – meets monthly with representation from Finance, Treasury, Product, Legal, and the Regional Ops Heads. All multiplier changes require **dual sign‑off** (data‑science recommendation + CFO approval). --- ## 10. KPI Dashboard – What Investors Will See | KPI (USD‑normalized) | Target | Frequency | Data Source | |----------------------|--------|-----------|-------------| | **EMP (Effective Monthly Price)** | ≥ $4.00 (weighted avg) | Weekly | Billing Engine | | **Gross Margin %** | 66 % +/- 2 pp | Monthly | Finance (post‑FX conversion) | | **CAC (USD)** | ≤ $30 (incl. family‑plan) | Quarterly | Marketing Attribution | | **LTV (USD)** | ≥ $200 | Annually | Cohort Analysis | | **Contribution Margin (LTV‑CAC)** | ≥ $150 | Quarterly | Finance | | **Churn (monthly)** | ≤ 5 % (overall) | Monthly | Product Analytics | | **FX‑Adjustment (USD)** | ≤ 2 % of revenue | Monthly | Treasury | | **Payment‑Completion Rate** | ≥ 97 % | Weekly | Payment Ops | | **Family‑Plan Penetration** | ≥ 30 % of paid users in LAT‑AM & SA | Quarterly | CRM | These figures will sit on the **Investor Relations “Pricing‑Health” slide deck**, updated each earnings call. --- ## 11. Sample Market‑Specific Pricing Tables | Country | Tier | Local Currency Price | EMP (USD) | Payment Options | |---------|------|----------------------|-----------|-----------------| | **Kenya** | Basic (SD) | KES 150 | $1.27 | M‑Pesa weekly top‑up (10‑day) | | | Standard (HD) | KES 300 | $2.55 | M‑Pesa + QR daily | | | Family (Standard) | KES 525 | $4.46 | Primary payer via M‑Pesa, up to 5 users | | **India** | Basic | INR 199 | $2.38 | UPI, credit‑card instalments (4‑mo) | | | Standard | INR 399 | $4.77 | UPI, credit‑card instalments | | | Family (Standard, 4‑6 users) | INR 649 | $7.76 | Primary wallet (PayTM) + OTP | | | Weekly Pass (Basic) | INR 49 | $0.59 | Mobile‑wallet pre‑pay | | **Brazil** | Basic | BRL 19 | $3.68 | Debit‑card, “boleto” (post‑paid) | | | Standard | BRL 37 | $7.16 | Debit‑card, 12‑month instalments | | | Premium | BRL 65 | $12.60 | Credit‑card, 6‑mo instalments | | | Family (Premium) | BRL 112 | $21.70 | Primary payer (debit) + up to 6 users | *All prices include the applicable **VAT/Digital‑Services Tax** and are rounded to the nearest 0.5 unit of local currency.* --- ## 12. Communication & Brand Narrative 1. **“Your Price, Your Reality”** – Emphasise that the company is *localising* to meet **income realities** while preserving *global quality*. 2. **Transparency Statement** – Publish the **pricing‑multiplier methodology** on the corporate site (interactive chart). 3. **Customer‑Education** – In‑app tutorial: “How we calculate your monthly price”. Show the **USD reference** side‑by‑side with the local price to build trust. 4. **Investor Deck** – Dedicated slide “Local‑Pricing Engine” explaining the multiplier, FX‑hedge, and unit‑economics preservation. Use **scenario‑analysis charts** (like the table in Section 7). --- ## 13. TL;DR – The Core Play 1. **Set a global USD reference price** for each tier (Basic / Standard / Premium). 2. **Apply a transparent, data‑driven multiplier** (PPP × elasticity × tax × FX‑buffer) to generate a **local‑currency price** that respects income levels and payment‑rail costs. 3. **Integrate local payment rails** (mobile‑money, QR, instalments) with **auto‑conversion & hedging** so the company still reports in USD and keeps FX risk under control. 4. **Offer modular family‑sharing plans** priced as a multiple of the solo EMP; treat the whole family as one contract for CAC/LTV purposes. 5. **Standardise all financial reporting on “Effective Monthly Price”** and show margins, CAC, LTV, and an **FX‑adjustment line**; this delivers a **single, comparable unit‑economics story** to investors. 6. **Govern through a Global Pricing & Localization Committee**, use a real‑time dashboard, and run quarterly “price‑health” updates for the board. By executing this framework the Company can **unlock high‑growth, price‑sensitive markets** while **maintaining a disciplined, investor‑friendly financial narrative**.
